ing: unsalted, ground to a paste or powder
st: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 8 minutes with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add the onions and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and chile for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 8 minutes.
Add [[3 cups]] water, cover and simmer on low for 50 minutes until the beef is tender.
Mix the ground peanuts with [[0.5 cup]] of the hot stew liquid to a smooth paste, then stir it into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the stew is thick. Season with salt.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice. Boil it with [[1.5 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes.
Serve the stew over the rice.
Put the couscous in a bowl. Pour [[2 cups]] hot water over it with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, cover, and wait 10 minutes.
Fluff it with a fork so the grains separate.
Steam the couscous over simmering water in a steamer for 10 minutes, so it becomes light.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the moringa or spinach, the tomato, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pepper. Cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Toss the vegetables and crushed peanuts through the warm couscous. Taste and add salt.
Serve the dambou warm, on its own or beside grilled meat.
Freeze the beef for 30 minutes to make it firm, then slice very thin against the grain.
Lay the slices on trays and dry in the oven at 175°F (80°C) for 1 hour.
Mix the ground peanuts, cayenne, ginger, onion, garlic powder, paprika, salt, oil and [[3 tbsp]] water to a thick paste.
Coat each slice with the paste on both sides.
Return the slices to the oven at 175°F (80°C) and dry for 2 hours, turning once.
Raise the heat to 400°F (200°C) and roast for 8 minutes, or broil, to finish cooking the beef through.
Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Mix the millet flour with the ginger, pepper and salt. Add [[0.75 cup]] water and stir to form a thick dough.
Bring [[2 cups]] water to a boil. Roll the dough into golf-ball-size balls and drop them in.
Cook for 20 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Lift the balls out with a slotted spoon and mash them in a bowl into a smooth, sticky dough.
Shape into small walnut-size balls, with wet hands, and let them cool for 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, milk and sugar in a large bowl or pitcher.
Crumble or place the balls into the yogurt mixture and break them up with a spoon.
Serve the fura cold in cups or bowls with a spoon.
Mix the grated onion, garlic, cayenne, paprika, salt, black pepper and oil in a bowl.
Add the beef cubes and toss well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes in the fridge.
Soak the skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Thread the beef onto the skewers.
Heat a grill or broiler to high heat.
Cook the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with sliced raw onion, extra cayenne and bread.
Soak the raw rice in water for 4 hours, then drain.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar into the warm water and wait 5 minutes.
Blend the soaked rice, cooked rice and yeast water to a thick, smooth batter.
Pour into a bowl, cover and leave in a warm spot to ferment for 2 hours.
Stir in the remaining sugar, salt and baking powder. The batter should be like thick pancake batter.
Heat a pan with small round molds (a dimpled pan or well-greased muffin tin) with a little oil in each.
Fill each mold about three-quarters full. Cook on medium for 4 minutes until the underside is crisp and golden.
Flip and cook 3 minutes more. Serve warm.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add [[2 cups]] water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the okra and cook for 8 minutes more until tender. Season with salt.
Rinse the rice, then cook in [[2.5 cups]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes.
Rest the rice for 5 minutes, fluff, and serve under the sauce.
